picks.headline: Spotify's AI-powered audiobook narration opens up to all authors
picks.excerpt: Spotify is opening its AI audiobook narration program to all authors, using ElevenLabs voice models to produce the audio at no cost and with no exclusivity requirement — a direct challenge to Audible/ACX economics for indie authors.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability in the pool: a free, non-exclusive AI narration route that changes an author's audiobook decision this week.

picks.headline: Publishing's AI Reckoning
picks.excerpt: PW's cover feature on how the book business is learning to live with generative AI, for better and worse: HarperCollins moving to automate overseas translation, Wiley booking $49M in AI licensing revenue in FY2026, and editorial teams absorbing AI into everyday production.
picks.rationale: PW cover feature with hard numbers (Wiley's $49M AI licensing line, HarperCollins translation automation) that set the industry baseline.

picks.headline: 50 Things Every AI Working With Humans Should Know — Ken Liu's machine-assisted story
picks.excerpt: Lit Hub publishes Ken Liu's new story, written in explicit collaboration with AI systems and accompanied by an interview explaining the method — a rare documented craft record of literary co-writing rather than a disclosure scandal.
picks.rationale: Rare primary artifact: a major author publishing an AI-co-written story plus the method behind it, not another disclosure controversy.

picks.headline: Ingram's AI Rollout Is a Success
picks.excerpt: Fifteen months into deploying AI across its operations, Ingram says the technology is already changing how the distributor does business — from metadata and customer service to print-on-demand workflow decisions.
picks.rationale: Supply-side evidence with a 15-month track record — metadata and print-on-demand workflow changes that reach every publisher selling through Ingram.

picks.headline: What Machines Can't Replace: Why AI Makes Us More Human, with Anna McPhee
picks.excerpt: Software engineer, author and creative technologist Anna McPhee walks through an author workflow that uses AI for research, editing, admin and marketing while every word of the book stays human-written — a concrete division-of-labour model for creative work.
picks.rationale: A concrete, copyable division of labour between AI and human craft — the only workflow-level pick, balancing four industry/litigation-leaning stories.
